premises.scope: Partner pair/triple stitching for flat exceptional direction; used as the named completed partner mechanism to extend.
Definite principal-pair density bound pi/sqrt(|det|), nonsingular principal-triple bound (2pi+3sqrt(3))/sigma_min, both uniform under affine tilts and outside-coordinate conditioning.
Previous arbitrary-orientation but equal-baseline codimension-one theorem; the present result removes its equality/rank-one structure.

proved_result.statement: If n>=4 and at least n-1 eigenvalues of a real symmetric A are all <=-L or all >=L, L>0, with the remaining eigenvalue arbitrary, then for independent density<=1 coordinates the density of X^T A X is bounded by C_same/L, where C_same=max(pi*sqrt(1000/17),(2000/949)*(2*pi+3*sqrt(3)))<24.193. No equality, cluster, exceptional-direction, moment, support, or rotated-independence assumption is used.
proved_result.local_lemma: For any 4x4 symmetric block with lambda_3<=-L, either a principal negative-definite pair has determinant >=(17/1000)L^2 or every principal triple has sigma_min >=(949/2000)L. The proof uses Cauchy interlacing and e2(T)=sum of the three principal pair determinants, with 3*(17/1000)+2*(949/2000)=1.

unresolved_implication: The full hypothesis gives only three arbitrary large eigendirections, not n-1 same-sign large eigenvalues. Diffuse rank-three projectors defeat selection of a uniformly conditioned fixed physical triple, while mixed-sign hyperbolic blocks defeat the pair/triple dichotomy. A product-preserving aggregation of complementary local smoothers remains necessary.
next_step: Combine diffuse/separable-phase control with same-sign pair/triple and multi-pivot/hyperbolic mechanisms in an aggregate spectral-geometric dichotomy that pays total exterior-minor mass before reciprocal local conditioning.
